headline: High risk from Haystack’s broad network/MCP defaults; prompt-injection and cascading-error risks are limited by Awesome Python’s non-runnable, read-only profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack can call MCP servers and REST APIs by default, so it may ingest attacker-controlled content through shared channels. Awesome Python is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces, so it cannot itself inject content, but it can still be the source of copied instructions if manually bridged. The interaction is indirect, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Haystack is configured to read content from an MCP server or REST source that includes untrusted text
IF a human copies content from Awesome Python into Haystack as instructions
mitigations: Disable MCP sources that are not provenance-tagged
Restrict Haystack to allowlisted REST endpoints
Require a human review step before any instruction-like text is executed
Use separate workspaces for copied content
requires-engineering: add provenance filtering for retrieved text

B_data_leakage.rationale: Awesome Python touches no data classes and has no network egress, while Haystack only lists anonymous usage statistics and broad egress. There is no shared workspace or secret-handling evidence, so a leakage path is not documented. The main concern is accidental transmission from Haystack, but the pair itself does not show sensitive data flow.
conditions: IF Haystack is pointed at sensitive documents outside the documented anonymous-usage scope
IF both agents are placed in a shared workspace with unredacted files
mitigations: Keep Haystack inputs limited to non-sensitive content
Run the agents in separate directories
Disable any optional telemetry beyond anonymous usage stats
Review outbound destinations before enabling connectors
requires-engineering: enforce data-class filtering at ingestion

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Awesome Python is not runnable and requests no permissions, so it cannot contend for writes. Haystack is runnable and can call APIs, but no filesystem write, git, or shared mutable-resource capability is documented. Without overlapping write surfaces, capability conflict is limited to read-side coordination issues.
conditions: IF Haystack is extended with filesystem or git write access to the same directory as another agent
IF an orchestrator grants both agents the same mutable OAuth scope
mitigations: Keep Haystack read-only for shared resources
Do not grant shared OAuth scopes
Separate any writable directories
Document ownership of each mutable resource
requires-engineering: add locking for shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack can consume retrieved content and act through REST/MCP integrations, so if it treats upstream text as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions. Awesome Python is only a curated collection, not an executing agent, so it is not a direct actor; however, its content could still be copied into Haystack. The pathway exists but is not fully documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Haystack uses retrieved text from any source as authoritative without verification
IF downstream connectors are enabled to send emails, tickets, or API actions
mitigations: Add a verification step before any action-taking connector
Require citations for retrieved claims
Limit Haystack to read-only retrieval mode
Log and review all tool calls
requires-engineering: implement confidence thresholds for actions

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for Awesome Python, and Haystack only explicitly touches anonymous usage statistics. Because the pair lacks evidence of regulated data classes, compliance risk is limited to policy drift if operators route sensitive content through Haystack. The other agent is not cited for a specific violation because none is documented.
conditions: IF operators route regulated data through Haystack connectors
IF retention or logging settings differ from the operator’s policy
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through the pair
Review retention settings before deployment
Disable unnecessary logging
Keep a written data-flow inventory
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention
